title: Spectrum Symmetry Mirror
description: A clickable 16-bin DFT spectrum with connector arcs between conjugate pairs, showing why a real-valued input makes the upper half of the spectrum redundant.
creator: Real-Time DSP on a $5 Microcontroller
author: Dan McCreary
subject: Digital Signal Processing
DFT
Frequency Analysis

educational.topic: Conjugate symmetry of the DFT for real inputs
learningObjectives: Interpret the structure of a full N-point spectrum
Explain why bin k and bin N-k are conjugates for real input
Identify the two bins that are their own mirror
prerequisites: A DFT produces N complex outputs

controls.label: Any bin
controls.purpose: Draw the connector arc to its mirror and explain the pairing

controls.label: Clear selection
controls.purpose: Remove the arc and return to the prompt

limitations: Shows the index relationship only; actual bin values are not computed here

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Click-triggered connector arcs over a persistent layout
keyQuestions: Which bins have no separate partner, and why?
How many bins are unique for a real input?
commonMisconceptions: That all N bins carry independent information
That the upper half represents higher frequencies than Nyquist
assessmentOpportunities: Determine how many bins of a 256-point FFT need to be kept
